items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: he was the one who brought me there and he was the same as a father to me. I stayed in his house and ate and slept... What, the Fledgings band all the time? Yeah.

ctx.x: But I never was interested in nothing like none of them. I wanted to blow. I got me a clarinet. I was a clarinet. And nobody learned me nothing about that. I just found all the cards. I mean all the new things I wanted to find myself. But my daddy didn't know nothing about it. And nobody around here. There was a fellow around here named Piku. White from the barber here. Here, after I began to practice and clearly, he called me up to his barber shop and he showed me a whole lot of this, you know, tech things on…
His name was 피Cu Lazana. 피Cu Lazana. 피Cu Lazana. Yeah. He was a barber here.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: I started playing with Tom Albert... I was with him from 1918 up to 1924... I lived right there with them.

ctx.x: Oh, wow. I just wanted to get him straight. Yeah. So I'd know who he was.

Uh-huh. Then I played with Rene and he'd come over there. As a matter of fact, I played with Rene here. But he first known me from over there. Uh, when Jim Robson used to come over there with Sam Morgan, I was a little boy then. And he used to come over there with Sam Morgan when I used to play with him. And then Isaiah Morgan made up him a band. He used to come over there. He used to play with him. I played with Isaiah a long time. And then Tom Albert come to play with my daddy. Well, he told me I was a heard me…
What kind of cornet did he play? Did he play straight or hard?
